heroHeadline: Pact Gets Its First Leader as Chiefs of Staff Rush to Riyadh After New Houthi Missile Barrage
heroSubtitle: Pakistan named retired Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood as the Mecca pact's first secretary-general on Sep 23, giving the seven-week-old alliance its first named institutional face. The appointment landed just as the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted six Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Taif and Yanbu on Sep 24, prompting foreign ministers Faisal bin Farhan, Ishaq Dar and Hakan Fidan to meet in New York, condemn the attacks, and agree to an urgent chiefs-of-staff meeting. By Sep 25, Turkey's and Pakistan's top generals were en route to Riyadh — the pact's fastest institutional movement yet, though Turkey's Fidan signaled any help would be "technical" rather than combat forces, and a Houthi spokesman warned Islamabad and Ankara of an "iron fist" if they intervene directly.
